diagnostic_evidence.quote: provides a necessary condition of it
Let $\left\Vert \cdot\right\Vert $ be any given norm on $\mathbb{R}^{2}$.

issues.failure_explanation: Moments of the exponential model are governed by coordinatewise one-sided conditions such as int_{||z||>1} e^{k z^{(i)}} l(dz) < infinity. An O(e^{-B||z||}) bound with k<B is therefore sufficient, not necessary, so the 'if and only if' with e^{k||z||} and both 'necessary' claims are false. B_ell also depends on the arbitrarily chosen norm: rescaling the norm rescales B_ell, so 'B_ell>2' is not a meaningful condition for 'any given norm'. Concretely, in the rho-norm used for NTS, B_ell = 2*lambda/(sqrt(||eta||^2+2*lambda)+||eta||) <= sqrt(2*lambda) = sqrt(2) < 2 for VG0 (lambda=1), and this rate is attained along z parallel to eta. Yet the NTS exponent gives lambda - u^T eta - u^T rho u/2 > 0 for u = 2e_1, 2e_2, (1,1), so VG0 has finite second moments. VG0 thus refutes the necessity claim and violates the paper's own standing assumption.

failure_location.quote: the stronger condition $B_{\ell}\geq2$ is necessary to guarantee the

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the condition with a sufficient coordinatewise exponential-moment condition (e.g. int_{||z||>1} e^{2z^{(i)}} l(dz) < infinity and the analogous condition for e^{z^{(1)}+z^{(2)}}). Fix the norm or drop 'B_ell>2', and delete the 'iff'/'necessary' statements.
issues.overall_effect: The stated modelling assumptions and scope are internally inconsistent with the VG0 experiment, and the claimed role of B_ell is wrong. The numerical scheme does not use B_ell, so no formal result is invalidated.
issues.title: Exponential-decay/moment condition misstated; VG0 test set violates the standing assumption B_ell>2
issues.why_classification: A local restatement of the assumptions suffices. No derivation, algorithm or numerical result depends on B_ell.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: a damping procedure is used where the first time step (i.e.
$n=1$) is replaced by four time steps of size equal to $\frac{1}{4}h_{t}$
Our complete algorithm for the numerical solution of problem
and compute the ILU factorization of $I-h_{t}\theta\left(D-r_{\omega}I\right)$

issues.failure_explanation: The text replaces the first Crank-Nicolson step by four theta=1 steps of size h_t/4 to cope with the non-smooth payoff. Those steps need a different system matrix I-(h_t/4)(D-r_omega I), its own ILU factorization, a departure grid and T^SL for step h_t/4, and theta=1 in the fixed-point iteration. Algorithm 1 instead fixes theta=1/2 for every n=1..N_t and precomputes only one factorization and one T^SL. Executed as written, it performs undamped semi-Lagrangian CN from non-smooth data, which is not the scheme whose results are reported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add to Algorithm 1 the damping stage for n=1: four theta=1 steps of size h_t/4, each with its own matrix, ILU factorization and T^SL.
issues.overall_effect: The algorithm's stated procedure does not match the method used in the experiments. Its implied accuracy for non-smooth payoffs, for prices and Greeks, is not supported as written.
issues.title: Algorithm 1, presented as the complete algorithm, omits the damped start-up steps the scheme uses
issues.why_classification: The missing stage is fully specified in the text, so inserting it is a routine local completion. No result changes.

issues.failure_explanation: Var[B(G(t))] = E[G(t)]rho + Var[G(t)]eta eta^T = t*delta*Gamma(1-alpha)*lambda^{alpha-1}*rho + t*delta*Gamma(2-alpha)*lambda^{alpha-2}*eta eta^T. This equals the appendix formula with rho*lambda/(1-alpha). The Section 4 display has rho*lambda^{1-alpha} instead, which agrees only for alpha=0. For NIG0 (alpha=1/2) the displayed formula gives a standard deviation of about 0.021, not the tabulated 0.1958; the table value matches the appendix formula.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: reveal favourable second-order convergence of our method whenever the exponential
indicate that our method achieves favourable second-order convergence whenever the exponential

issues.failure_explanation: NIG0 and NIG1 have alpha=1/2, so A_ell=1. Here l ~ ||z||^{-3}, so int ||z|| l(dz) ~ int r^{-1} dr diverges: by the paper's own criterion these sets have infinite variation. Section 4 nevertheless claims second order for all four sets, including this regime. The abstract and conclusions restrict the observed second order to finite-variation models, which would be pointless if the infinite-variation sets also showed it. Hence either the NIG results do not exhibit second order and Section 4 overclaims, or the headline qualifier misstates the evidence. Moreover, only alpha=0 is tested among finite-variation NTS, and no error analysis is provided. The two statements cannot both describe the same regression results.

failure_location.quote: Clearly, the favourable result is found that the numerical scheme achieves second-order convergence for each set of parameters.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Report the regression orders p per parameter set and restate the claims consistently across Section 4, abstract and conclusions. For example: second order observed for VG; NIG orders as actually observed. Qualify 'whenever finite-variation' as an observation based on alpha=0 only.
issues.overall_effect: The reported convergence order for the NIG (infinite-variation) sets, and hence the advertised scope of second-order behaviour, is unreliable.
issues.title: Second-order convergence asserted for all sets, including infinite-variation NIG, contradicting the finite-variation qualifier
issues.why_classification: The repair requires no new method or proof architecture. It does entail a limited weakening of the main empirical accuracy claim for the infinite-variation NIG cases that the paper emphasizes.
